channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Treasury Buybacks Fail to Calm Bond Market
item.description: The Treasury’s surprise decision to at least double buybacks of longer-dated US debt briefly pushed yields lower, but much of that move quickly reversed as investors questioned whether the intervention can overcome inflation and fiscal concerns. PIMCO Executive VP, Market Strategist and Generalist Portfolio Manger Tony Crescenzi and Host of Bloomberg Money Tom Keene join Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss how markets are now looking to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech for clues on rates and how the central bank will respond to Treasury’s increasingly active role in the bond market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iceland Faces Close Vote on EU Talks
item.description: Iceland will vote August 29th on whether to resume accession talks with the European Union, with recent polling showing a narrow advantage for the “yes” side. RUV Correspondent Ingólfur Bjarni Sigfússon joins Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that debate is being shaped by security concerns, economic uncertainty and Iceland’s strategic position in the North Atlantic, while opponents warn about sovereignty and control over fisheries. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Harry, Meghan Head Back to Britain After Six Years
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle plan to return to Britain with Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet after six years in the US, with their children set to begin school there in September. Bloomberg News Reporter Tiwa Adebayo explains to David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that the surprise move brings Harry closer to King Charles as he undergoes cancer treatment, while questions remain over the family’s security and Harry’s strained relationship with Prince William. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Has No Easy Fix for What’s Really Driving Bond Yields Up
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent came to office blasting his predecessor for trying to re-engineer the world’s largest bond market. This week he took a stab at it himself.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Michael MacKenzie

item.title: US Push to Isolate Iran Runs Into China
item.description: The Trump administration is preparing additional measures to isolate Iran’s economy, but further pressure could mean targeting China, the dominant buyer of Iranian oil. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the situation with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini is Bloomberg News Senior Editor Wendy Benjaminson. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ‘It’s a Carry World’: EM Trade Notches Longest Run Since 2008
item.description: Cathy Hepworth, who heads $1.5 trillion asset manager PGIM’s emerging-markets debt team, doesn’t hesitate when asked about her highest-conviction theme across the developing world: “Carry, carry, carry.”
item.dc:creator: Vinícius Andrade and Srinivasan Sivabalan

item.title: Can Canada Still Trust America on Trade?
item.description: Chrystia Freeland says a tentative US-Canada trade agreement may prevent new US tariffs from taking effect, but only if Canada makes major concessions including easing retaliation, allowing US alcohol back into provincial stores and aligning with Washington on some digital issues. Existing US tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum, cars and auto parts would remain, though at lower levels. Freeland says that would mark a major shift from Canada’s long-held position that such tariffs violate USMCA, and could hurt both countries, especially US manufacturing and the Detroit-Windsor auto supply chain. This interview was recorded on Aug. 20. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi Oil Logistics Roiled Again by Houthis’ Red Sea Threat
item.description: Saudi Arabia is yet again being forced to overhaul how its oil gets to customers around the world, as Yemen’s Houthis make it harder for Riyadh to use a backup route that’s been vital to the global economy since the Iran war started.
item.dc:creator: Yongchang Chin, Weilun Soon, Prejula Prem and Grant Smith

item.title: Europe’s Luxury Giants Discern Green Shoots in Key China Market
item.description: Europe’s biggest luxury firms are turning a little more positive on the crucial Chinese market, as a fragile spending recovery takes shape in the country.
item.dc:creator: Chloé Meley

item.title: F1 Reviews China Boy Band’s Logo for Similarities: Global Times
item.description: The Formula One group is reviewing and investigating information about a logo used in a concert tour by Chinese boy group Teens in Times, after fans alleged it resembled F1’s trademark, the Global Times reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Mexican Governor Wanted by US Over Cartel Ties Seeks Leave Again
item.description: The Mexican governor accused by the US of conspiring with a cartel and abetting drug trafficking has once again requested leave, after returning to his post on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch

item.title: Australia Reports First Bird Flu Case in a Mammal as Seal Dies
item.description: Australia reported its first confirmed case of the H5 bird flu in a mammal, after a long-nosed fur seal was found dead in South Australia.
item.dc:creator: Edward Johnson

item.title: India Rescues Two of Ship’s 24 Crew Members After Distress Alert
item.description: India launched search-and-rescue operations for crew members of cargo ship MV OCEAN WINNER in the Bay of Bengal after receiving a distress alert on Aug. 22.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Mishra

item.title: New Zealand Opposition Vows to Restore RBNZ Dual Mandate
item.description: New Zealand’s main opposition Labour Party pledged to restore the central bank’s dual mandate if it wins office in the Nov. 7 election, saying price stability and sustainable employment are both essential for a strong economy.
item.dc:creator: Edward Johnson

item.title: Malaysia Rules Out $1.9 Billion Takeover of Passport Supplier
item.description: Malaysia’s government has ruled out a potential acquisition of Datasonic Technologies Sdn., which supplies the country’s passports and national identity cards.
item.dc:creator: Netty Ismail

item.title: Korean Traders Chase 40% Coupons as Risk Appetite Survives Rout
item.description: A historic stock selloff has driven South Korea’s retail investors toward complex structured products as the risk-loving cohort continues to look for ways to boost returns.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Bloomberg Previews Jackson Hole Symposium
item.description: Bloomberg's Joe Weisenthal, Lisa Abramowicz, Tracy Alloway and Tom Keene preview the Jackson Hole Symposium as all eyes will be on Fed Chairman Kevin Marsh and his first annual symposium address. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Juicy Yields Draw Junk Bond Buyers to Investment-Grade AI Debt
item.description: Companies looking to finance data center projects are increasingly turning to junk bond investors to help them raise billions of dollars, even for debt that is investment-grade.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 8/22/2026
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Alexis Christoforous bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Former MI6 Chief Sir Richard Dearlove, American Whiskey Association President & CEO Michael Bilello, The Atlantic Contributing Writer and Columbia University Institute of Global Politics Distinguished Fellow Kim Ghattas, and Carleton College Professor of Economics and “Demographics and the Demand for Higher Education” Author Nathan Grawe. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Alexis Christoforous, David Gura, and Christina Ruffini as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)
